summary: Angler fighting a fish with a spinning rod: rod butt against the belly, rod raised about 50-60 degrees and bent deeply, right hand on the fore grip, left hand cranking the reel, knees bent and leaning back.

rules.why: knees bent, body leaning back against the pull
leaning back with a straight back

text.action: an angler fighting a strong fish, pumping the bent rod
text.core: Knees bent and body leaning back; rod butt tucked against the belly, rod raised about 55 degrees and bent deeply toward the fish; right hand on the fore grip above the reel, left hand turning the spinning reel handle under the rod; line taut to the water.
text.gaze: Eyes on the line where it enters the water.
cues: keep the rod at 45-60 degrees above the water
lift the rod, then reel while lowering it
smooth, small pumping strokes, never let the line go slack
kinetic: rod bending into a deep arc
line taut and cutting the water, spray where the fish pulls
avoid: line not ending in the water

sources.cite: takemefishing.org: fight with the rod about 45 deg to the water, pump up toward vertical and reel while lowering; spinning reel hangs under the rod
Pakula: lifting past about 60 deg above horizontal gains no line; pressure position 45-60 deg (search extract)
